specificationContent.para: Alerts are classified into three priority levels based on severity and required crew response time per CS-25.1322 and SAE ARP4102 guidelines.

row.entry: Fire, engine failure, flight control malfunction, terrain alert
Crew awareness and timely action needed
Low fuel, hydraulic pressure low, door not locked, cabin altitude
System mode change, configuration status, operational reminders

specificationContent.para: Certain alerts may be suppressed or inhibited during specific flight phases to reduce crew workload and prevent nuisance alerts:
Takeoff Phase (Power application to 400 ft AGL or 60 seconds):
- Suppress: Low-priority configuration advisories, non-essential system messages
- Allow: All warnings, essential cautions related to flight safety
Landing Phase (Below 800 ft AGL to touchdown):
- Suppress: Non-essential cautions, maintenance advisories
- Allow: Terrain alerts, landing configuration warnings, critical system failures
Ground Operations:
- Allow: All alerts including maintenance-related messages
- Special handling: Master caution/warning lights remain illuminated until acknowledged

specificationSpec.specificationTitle: Alert Message Queuing and Display Priority

specificationContent.para: When multiple alerts are active simultaneously, display priority follows these rules:
1. Level 1 (WARNING) messages shall always be displayed first and in full view
2. Level 2 (CAUTION) messages displayed after warnings, in chronological order
3. Level 3 (ADVISORY) messages displayed last, may be abbreviated if space limited
4. Maximum simultaneous messages displayed: 12 (configurable per aircraft type)
5. Overflow messages accessible via scrolling with overflow indicator present
6. Acknowledged messages move to secondary list but remain accessible for review
7. Repeated messages increment occurrence counter rather than creating duplicate entries
Aural alerts shall meet the following requirements:
Warning Level Aural Alerts:
- Continuous tone: 400-800 Hz, modulated if appropriate to alert type
- Voice alerts: Clear synthetic or recorded voice stating emergency condition
- Volume: Minimum 75 dB, adjustable up to 90 dB at pilot ear position
- Duration: Continuous until crew acknowledgement or condition cleared
Caution Level Aural Alerts:
- Single chime: 500-1000 Hz, duration 0.5-1.0 seconds
- Volume: Minimum 70 dB at pilot ear position
- Repetition: Single chime on initial alert, no repeat unless new caution occurs
Advisory Level:
- No aural alert required
- Optional: Soft click or low-volume tone if desired for specific advisories
Alert acknowledgement shall follow these procedures:
1. Master Warning Light: Press to acknowledge, silences aural, transfers alerts to message list
2. Master Caution Light: Press to acknowledge, silences aural if active, clears light when all cautions addressed
3. Individual Message Cancel: Not permitted for active warnings or cautions
4. Message Review: Acknowledged messages remain in history for flight duration
5. Persistent Alerts: Reappear if condition persists after initial acknowledgement
6. Post-Flight Review: All alerts logged to QAR and maintenance system for analysis
